answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using hardware remote attestation. Agents exchange cryptographic enclave proofs across a peer whisper network, anchoring identities to a basalt ledger. This forces an adversary to incur the verifiable cost of purchasing unique physical secure chips across an infrastructure orchard rather than running cheap virtual machines. However, the system relies on centralized silicon vendors and remains susceptible to microarchitectural side-channel leaks.
